solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Faith in one possible outcome after last trump's played

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

parts.words: possible outcome after last trump's played
parts.note: in bridge a slam, winning every trick or all but one, is what may follow once the last trump is played

explanation.surface: Someone trusts that the final trump card, once played, will bring about the result they hope for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last trump' also suggests Judgement Day, which suits a clue about faith, but here it is the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is one of the world's major religions, and a faith is a religion.

clue.text: A centrist actively establishing networks

indicators.note: acting busily, so the letters of 'A centrist' are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A middle-of-the-road politician is busily building up contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Networking means mixing and dealing with others socially or professionally, which is what someone who interacts does.

clue.text: City lights using too much energy?

indicators.note: the lights take in a surplus letter for energy, one more than they already have

parts.note: LEDs are light-emitting diodes, small electric lights
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A complaint about a city's illuminations wasting power.
explanation.walkthrough: LEDS already holds one E; 'using too much energy' adds a second inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Severely cut capital raised on account

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it
in a down clue, raised means the shortened city is read upwards, from bottom to top
cut short, so the final letter of the city is lopped off

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a tally is a running account or score

explanation.surface: Money raised against an account has been drastically reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Severely cut' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Severely'. ROME cut gives ROM, raised gives MOR, above TALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortally wounded means fatally or gravely hurt, so the adverb conveys extreme seriousness.

clue.text: One may receive sentence in absence of hearing?

definitions.text: One may receive sentence in absence of hearing?

parts.words: One may receive sentence in absence of hearing
parts.note: sounds like a defendant sentenced without a court hearing, but describes a deaf person following spoken sentences by watching the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' and 'hearing' point to the courtroom; the real sense is words understood without sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A lip-reader understands speech by watching the speaker's mouth movements, often because they cannot hear.

clue.text: Nearly all wanting change of leader vanished without trace

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: most means nearly all

explanation.surface: Almost everyone who wanted a new party leader has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of leader' only says the first letter changes; the new letter L comes from the definition and crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lost has disappeared and cannot be found, gone without a trace.

clue.text: Liberal young woman charges for a topless dance

parts.note: per means for each or for a, as in 'five pounds per ticket'
miss is a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: without its top, so the dance loses its first letter

parts.note: the jive is a lively dance

explanation.surface: A young woman is paid to perform a topless dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' joins the pieces: MISS charges PER, i.e. a price 'per' something, with IVE after.
explanation.definitionFit: A permissive attitude is a tolerant, liberal one that allows freedom of behaviour.

clue.text: Take on space manoeuvre

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
a ploy is a cunning manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Attempting a manoeuvre in outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on staff is to hire them, which is what employing means.

clue.text: Stray into fight, yielding quarter finally in heroic action

indicators.note: the straying goes inside the shortened fight
giving up its final quarter, so the last two of the fight's eight letters go

parts.note: a ding-dong is a noisy fight or argument
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Someone wanders into a brawl and ends up giving quarter, in a brave deed.
explanation.walkthrough: DINGDONG loses its final quarter (NG) to leave DINGDO, and ERR goes inside after the D. 'Quarter' looks like mercy or a compass point; here it is a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is an old word for daring, heroic exploits.

clue.text: Amateur soldiers dressed up for real once

indicators.note: in a down clue, put upward, so the joined pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: lay means non-professional, amateur
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Part-time soldiers put on their dress uniform for a genuine occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'real once' marks an archaic sense: in old English 'real' could mean royal, as in real tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage 'real' meant regal or kingly, a sense surviving in 'real tennis'.

clue.text: Gold is supplanting diamonds in European articles for the speculator

indicators.note: taking the place of, so the gold piece pushes out the diamonds

parts.note: THE is the English definite article and DER the German one
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold replacing diamonds in European goods sounds like a market speculator's tip.
explanation.walkthrough: THE + DER are the two articles; replace DER's D with OR + IS to give THE + ORIS + ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A theoriser speculates, forming theories and conjectures rather than proven facts.

clue.text: Company salary about right?

indicators.note: the salary goes around the abbreviation for right

parts.note: pay is salary

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a firm's pay is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A party is a group of people, as in 'a party of walkers', so it is company in that sense.

clue.text: Some bounder — a scallywag?

definitions.meaning: first sense: a cad, a dishonourable man

indicators.note: only some of the letters across these words are taken, a run spanning their joins

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a cad might also be a scamp.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'bounder a scallywag'; both 'bounder' and 'scallywag' also define it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or scamp, so both a cad and a mischievous person fit.

clue.text: Symbolic expression of albino cycling around a motorway?

indicators.note: the rotated word goes around the motorway
the first letters are rotated round to the end of the word

parts.note: taken as written
the M1 is a British motorway, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An albino cyclist riding round a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling ALBINO moves AL to the end, giving BINOAL; that goes around MI to make BINO-MI-AL. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A binomial is an algebraic expression of two terms, such as x + y, written in symbols.

clue.text: Terrified of ploughing fifth grade?

indicators.note: ploughing turns the soil over, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A child scared of failing in the fifth grade at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifth grade' looks like a school year; it is only the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Affrighted is an old word for frightened or scared.

clue.text: Couple of minutes missing from much test film shot in sepia

indicators.note: these letters are absent from the anagram's letters
shot as in ruined, so the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: two Ms, M being the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A photography note about a long test film shot in sepia tones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sepia' seems to be a colour for the film; it is also the Latin genus name of the cuttlefish, whose ink gave the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the zoological genus of the common cuttlefish, the source of sepia ink.

clue.text: Figures out integrals

indicators.note: out as in disordered, so the letters of integrals are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone works out integrals in a calculus problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures out' reads as one phrase meaning works out; split it, and 'Figures' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Triangles are geometric shapes, and shapes are called figures in geometry.

clue.text: How long could it take Rishi to consign Boris's backing to the far right?

indicators.note: to consign is to send off, here sending the letter away from its place
the letter ends up at the extreme right-hand end of the word

parts.note: a rishi is a Hindu sage or seer
the back letter of Boris

explanation.surface: A political jibe: how long before Rishi Sunak sidelines Boris Johnson's supporters to the far right?
explanation.walkthrough: The British politicians are decoys: a rishi is a sage, and the S moves from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages means a very long time, the answer to how long something might take.

clue.text: Something fishy about stories of the first rank?

indicators.note: the fish goes about the stories

parts.note: a smelt is a small fish
lies are untrue stories

explanation.surface: Suspicions about top-class journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first rank' sounds like top quality; rank also means foul-smelling, so the first, most rank, is the smelliest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means having a strong unpleasant smell, so the highest degree of rankness is the most malodorous.

clue.text: Irritable blundering rector expelled from working copartnerships

indicators.note: the clergyman's letters go astray, in any order
these letters are thrown out of the longer word
the leftover letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy clergyman kicked out of business partnerships that were going well.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R, E, C, T, O, R out of COPARTNERSHIPS to leave PANSHIPS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappish describes someone sharp-tempered, quick to snap at others.

clue.text: Fit model in uniform? The opposite

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
reverses the order just stated, so the uniform letter goes inside the model word

parts.note: to sit is to pose as an artist's model
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fit model wearing a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model in uniform' would put SIT around U's contents; 'The opposite' flips it, so U goes inside SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit is to be appropriate or right for, as in 'that job will suit you'.

clue.text: Forced into new base after campaign

indicators.note: the base comes after the campaign and new

parts.note: a drive is an organised campaign
home is a base, as in home base

explanation.surface: Soldiers forced back to a new base after a military campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail or argument driven home is forced in firmly until it is fully embedded.

clue.text: Translate verse to be sung at Christmas?

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated DEC
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poem written to be sung as a Christmas carol.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode is to convert a coded message into plain language, a kind of translation.

clue.text: Tory fringe to reach agreement on something

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, i.e. Tory
a verge is an edge or fringe

explanation.surface: Members on the edge of the Conservative party trying to agree a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Views that converge come together, so people converging find common ground.

clue.text: Function carried out by medic producing devices to control shock

indicators.note: the function carries the medic within it

parts.note: cos is the trigonometric function cosine
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor performs a procedure that produces equipment for treating shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks medical; it is a shock of hair, an unruly mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Combs tidy hair, and a shock is a thick untidy mop of hair.

clue.text: Wind, sun and April storms

indicators.note: storms as a verb, rampages, so the letters of April are thrown about

explanation.surface: A weather report: wind, sunshine and April storms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is a verb here, to coil, not the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To spiral is to wind round and round in a coil.

clue.text: Some of it's ornately served up?

definitions.text: Some of it's ornately served up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters are read bottom to top
only some of the letters across these words are taken

explanation.surface: A dish, part of which is presented elaborately.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a potato dish that may be served up ornately.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of grated fried potato, something served at table.

clue.text: Afters from Iceland's milk — very popular?

definitions.text: Afters from Iceland's milk — very popular?

indicators.note: afters means the rear parts, so the last letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A dessert made from Icelandic milk that has become a big hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afters' is British for dessert and also signals the ends of words. The whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyr is a thick cultured dairy product from Iceland, often eaten as a pudding.

clue.text: Doctor backs endless sex here in Sweden

indicators.note: the doctor goes at the back of the shortened sex
without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: male is one of the sexes
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor supporting unlimited sex in permissive Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmö is a major port city in southern Sweden, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Disagree with recording children

parts.note: a take is one recording of a scene or song
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: Objecting to a recording that features children.
explanation.definitionFit: To take issue with someone is an idiom for disputing or arguing with them.

clue.text: I support litigant making case for pay out

indicators.note: the litigant forms a case around the paying out

parts.note: a suer is one who sues
to spend is to pay out

explanation.surface: A litigant arguing in favour of paying out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks as the answer: a suspender says 'I support', holding up stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is an elastic strap that holds up a stocking or sock, a kind of support.

clue.text: Raise hope — insist on joining halves together

indicators.note: one half is set on to the other, joined at its end
half of the word, here its first half
the second half of the other word, put together with the first piece

explanation.surface: Boosting hopes by insisting on unity.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first half of 'hope' (HO) and the second half of 'insist' (IST), and join them.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to lift something up, especially with ropes or tackle.
